p: This was one of the chief singers, 1Ch 16:41.
I will take heed to my: Although he had appointed with himself patiently to have wait for God's timing, yet the vehemency of his pain caused him to break his purpose.
and my sorrow was stirred: Though when the wicked ruled he thought to have kept silence, yet his zeal caused him to change his mind.
spake I with my tongue: He confesses that he grudged against God, considering the greatness of his sorrows, and the shortness of his life.
vanity: Yet David offended in that he reasoned with God as though he were too severe toward his weak creature.
foolish: Do not make me a laughing stock to the wicked, wrap me up with the wicked when they are put to shame.
thou didst it: Seeing my troubles came from your providence, I ought to have endured them patiently.
makest his: Though your open plagues do not light on them forever, yet your secret curse continually frets them.

beauty to consume away like a: The word signifies all that he desires, as health, force, strength, beauty, and in whatever he has delight, so that the rod of God takes away all that is desired in this world.

before I go hence: For his sorrow caused him to think that God would destroy him completely, by which we see how hard it is for the saints to keep a measure in their words, when death and despair assails them.
